raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Gemma-3 multimodal uses **bidirectional attention among image tokens** during prefill (text stays causal). In SGLang this is realized by `Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration.prepare_attn_masks()` building a dense per-sequence mask — but that path is gated to `TritonAttnBackend` only (see the note in `gemma3_mm.py`: *"only the TritonAttnBackend supports bidirectional attention; other backends have not yet implemented this"*).

On the Intel XPU attention backend the mask was never applied, so image tokens ran plain **causal** attention, degrading vision-heavy tasks while leaving text unaffected.

On Intel Arc Pro B60 (`--attention-backend intel_xpu`, tp1), `docvqa_val` ANLS:

| backend | ANLS |
|---|---|
| intel_xpu (before) | 59.4 |
| triton (same HW) | 64.1 |
| H200 (ref) | 65.0 |
| **intel_xpu (this PR, sgl-kernel-xpu native)** | **67.48** |

Text-only `gsm8k_cot` is unchanged between intel_xpu and triton, consistent with the gap being image-specific.

## Modifications

This does the bidirectional masking **in the kernel** (via sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#495), keeping the sglang path a normal flash-attn call — no attention fallback in the model runner.

- `models/gemma3_mm.py::prepare_attn_masks`: for `XPUAttentionBackend`, build a per extend-token block id (image index, `-1` for text) and store it on the backend (`is_xpu()`-guarded lazy import; the Triton path is unchanged). Full prefill only.
- `layers/attention/xpu_backend.py::forward_extend`: when present, run non-causal and pass `bidirectional_block_ids` to `flash_attn_with_kvcache`; the kernel re-imposes causal for block-less tokens and keeps same-block (image) tokens bidirectional. `window_size` is dropped for this path (short multimodal prefill: the sliding window is a no-op and would otherwise re-mask the block).
- `layers/layernorm.py::forward_xpu`: make the input contiguous before `gemma_rmsnorm` (it requires a contiguous last dim, which a sliced hidden state may not have) so Gemma-3 loads on XPU.

Depends on the companion kernel PR sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#495 (`bidirectional_block_ids`). Run with `--chunked-prefill-size -1` (full prefill).

## Accuracy

`docvqa_val` (lmms-eval, ANLS), Intel Arc Pro B60, tp1, `--enable-multimodal --attention-backend intel_xpu --chunked-prefill-size -1`: **59.4 → 67.48** over the full 5349-sample val set, above the H200 reference (65.0). `gsm8k_cot` (text) unchanged. The kernel is unit-tested against an fp32 reference on the companion PR.

## Checklist

- [x] Lint: ruff / ruff-format / isort clean.
- [x] Bidirectional prefill is prefill-only; decode / CUDA-graph paths are untouched.

nodes.body:
Updated this PR to the **native sgl-kernel-xpu** approach instead of the earlier torch/SDPA fallback, per the review (@mingfeima @airMeng). The sglang side is now thin, it builds a per extend-token image-block id and passes `mm_block_id` to `flash_attn_with_kvcache`; the bidirectional masking is done in the kernel.

Companion kernel PR: sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#495 (adds the `mm_block_id` prefill mask). This PR depends on it.

- `prepare_attn_masks`: for `XPUAttentionBackend`, build the block ids (image index, `-1` for text); Triton path unchanged.
- `forward_extend`: run non-causal + pass `mm_block_id`; the kernel re-imposes causal for text and keeps image tokens bidirectional.
- `layernorm.forward_xpu`: make the input contiguous before `gemma_rmsnorm` (needs a contiguous last dim) so Gemma-3 loads.

Accuracy unchanged from the fallback: `docvqa_val` (full 5349) **59.4 -> 67.5** on Intel Arc Pro B60, above H200 (65.0). Kernel unit test added on the kernel PR.

The `is_xpu()` import guard from the previous round is retained.

Gentle re-review request. The companion kernel PR (sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#495) has now merged, so the `bidirectional_block_ids` prefill mask this PR depends on is in sgl-kernel-xpu main, and the API here matches it. I've also rebased this branch onto current main (mergeable, CI-clean).

I believe the earlier concerns are addressed: the XPUAttentionBackend import is `is_xpu()`-guarded (no silent fallback to causal), and the earlier "torch fallback would be slow" point no longer applies since the masking is now done natively in the kernel rather than a Python SDPA path. Could you take another look when you have a moment? Happy to adjust anything.
if a native fallback attention is needed, can you implement it in sgl-kernel-xpu and keep the interface in sglang unchanged after the performant solution ready?

bidirectional goes to triton on CUDA side.
at the currrent moment, you can also do so.

later you can provide support from sgl-kernel-xpu.

use torch fallback would be very slow.

catching every exception while importing `XPUAttentionBackend` silently restores causal image attention, which is the incorrect behavior this PR fixes.

Guard the import with `is_xpu()` and let unexpected XPU import errors fail loudly.

I've checked the perf of the torch fallback here,  it's actually not slow, and comes out faster than routing to triton on XPU:

gemma-3-4b-it `docvqa_val` (B60, tp1, limit-20, `--chunked-prefill-size -1`):

| | intel_xpu + SDPA | triton |
|---|---|---|
| prefill wall span | ~21s | ~56s |
| end-to-end (24 reqs) | ~28s | ~86s |
| prefill tok/s (median/mean) | 420 / 1475 | 64 / 874 |

Further, I'm working on `sgl-kernel-xpu` support for the proper solution.

Done, gated the import on `is_xpu()` and dropped the `try/except` so a real XPU import error surfaces instead of silently falling back to causal. (renamed the local flag to `is_xpu_backend` to avoid shadowing the helper.) e858b35132

I think our implementation support in-contiguous output
https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/blob/ecddde5da12abfc752b0aa9523e5ffb0bc5391d7/src/sycl/RMSNorm.cpp#L955
extract as a single funtion to sgl-kernel.

Checked the kernel: gemma_rmsnorm handles non-contiguous batch strides, but still needs a contiguous last dim (a transposed input trips CHECK_LAST_DIM_CONTIGUOUS), which Gemma-3 hits here. Tightened the guard to only make it contiguous when stride(-1) != 1, so the batch-strided cases the kernel already handles stay untouched. Can move it kernel-side (relax the last-dim check in gemma_rmsnorm) if you prefer. PTAL.

Extracted to sgl-kernel-xpu as build_bidirectional_block_ids(seq_lens, block_spans, device) in sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#495. What stays here only reads the spans from ForwardBatch/MultimodalInputs and calls it (that part I feel can't move into the kernel package). PTAL.
which one is more effective: 1. reorder x. 2. fallback to native path if not contiguous, just like ```forward_cpu```

Reorder (option 1) should win here. It copies only when stride(-1) != 1 (no-op otherwise), then stays on the fused kernel and keeps identical numerics for contiguous and non-contiguous inputs. The native fallback skips the copy but runs the slower multi-op path and can diverge numerically from the fused kernel for those tokens. Kept the reorder; can switch to a forward_native fallback if you prefer. PTAL.
still some changes needed. And the kernel change is not in v0.3.0 release, need to wait for next release.

a non-zero `extend_prefix_lens` returns None, so chunked prefill / radix cache silently keeps causal image attention. Triton still builds the mask for a cached prefix. Raise if image tokens are present and this is not a full prefill.

Disabling the sliding window is only equivalent for short prefills, but the code does not enforce that bound. Preserve local-attention behavior for longer image prompts and add a focused XPU regression test.

@@ -136,8 +136,13 @@ def __init__(
                 "graph decode path cannot run the varlen KV gather."
             )
 
+        # Gemma-3 multimodal: per extend-token image-block id set by
+        # prepare_attn_masks each image EXTEND forward, consumed by forward_extend.
+        self.bidirectional_block_ids = None
+
     def init_forward_metadata(self, forward_batch: ForwardBatch):
         """Initialize forward metadata hence all layers in the forward pass can reuse it."""
+        self.bidirectional_block_ids = None
         metadata = FlashAttentionMetadata()
         seqlens_in_batch = forward_batch.seq_lens
         batch_size = forward_batch.batch_size
@@ -653,6 +658,23 @@ def forward_extend(
                 cu_seqlens_k = metadata.encoder_cu_seqlens_k
                 window_size = (-1, -1)
 
+            # Gemma-3 multimodal: prepare_attn_masks set bidirectional_block_ids (per
+            # extend-token image id, -1 for text). Run non-causal + pass it so the
+            # sgl-kernel-xpu prefill re-imposes causal for text but keeps image
+            # tokens bidirectional. window_size is dropped because multimodal
+            # prefill is short (<= sliding window, so the window is a no-op) and a
+            # (window, 0) local mask would re-mask the bidirectional image block.
+            causal_arg = False if use_cascade_attn else causal
+            bidirectional_block_ids = None
+            if (
+                self.bidirectional_block_ids is not None
+                and not layer.is_cross_attention
+                and not use_cascade_attn
+            ):
+                bidirectional_block_ids = self.bidirectional_block_ids
+                causal_arg = False
+                window_size = (-1, -1)
+
             result = flash_attn_with_kvcache(
                 q=q.contiguous().view(-1, layer.tp_q_head_num, layer.head_dim),
                 k_cache=key_cache,
@@ -663,9 +685,10 @@ def forward_extend(
                 cu_seqlens_k_new=None,
                 max_seqlen_q=max_seqlen_q,
                 softmax_scale=layer.scaling,
-                causal=False if use_cascade_attn else causal,
+                causal=causal_arg,
                 window_size=window_size,
                 softcap=layer.logit_cap,
+                bidirectional_block_ids=bidirectional_block_ids,
                 k_descale=k_descale,
                 v_descale=v_descale,
                 return_softmax_lse=use_cascade_attn,

@@ -1352,9 +1352,13 @@ def forward_xpu(self, x, residual: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None):
             # output and residual becomes x + residual for the next layer.
             gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm(x, residual, self.weight.data, self.eps)
             return x, residual
-        # The XPU kernel flattens leading dims internally, so 2D/3D/4D inputs
-        # can all go through it directly without a Python-side reshape.
+        # The XPU kernel flattens leading dims internally, so 2D/3D/4D inputs go
+        # through directly without a Python-side reshape. It handles
+        # non-contiguous batch/row strides but requires a contiguous last dim,
+        # which a permuted hidden state may not have.
         elif residual is None and x.dim() in (2, 3, 4):
+            if x.stride(-1) != 1:
+                x = x.contiguous()
             return gemma_rmsnorm(x, self.weight.data, self.eps)
         return self.forward_native(x, residual)

@@ -48,7 +48,7 @@
 )
 from sglang.srt.models.gemma3_causal import Gemma3ForCausalLM
 from sglang.srt.models.siglip import SiglipVisionModel
-from sglang.srt.utils import add_prefix
+from sglang.srt.utils import add_prefix, is_xpu
 from sglang.srt.utils.hf_transformers_utils import get_processor
 
 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
@@ -220,7 +220,8 @@ def prepare_attn_masks(
         mask_dtype: torch.dtype,
     ):
         """Prepare attention masks for multimodal inputs."""
-        if isinstance(get_attn_backend(), TritonAttnBackend):
+        backend = get_attn_backend()
+        if isinstance(backend, TritonAttnBackend):
             assert forward_batch.forward_mode == ForwardMode.EXTEND
             bidirectional_attn_masks_list = []
             bidirectional_attn_mask_indptr = torch.zeros(
@@ -271,6 +272,44 @@ def prepare_attn_masks(
                 get_attn_backend().forward_metadata.custom_mask = (
                     bidirectional_attn_masks
                 )
+        elif is_xpu():
+            # XPU takes a per extend-token image-block id (image index, -1 for
+            # text); the sgl-kernel-xpu FMHA prefill turns it into bidirectional
+            # image attention (see xpu_backend.forward_extend). Import lazily so
+            # non-XPU builds are unaffected.
+            from sglang.srt.layers.attention.xpu_backend import XPUAttentionBackend
+
+            if isinstance(backend, XPUAttentionBackend):
+                assert forward_batch.forward_mode == ForwardMode.EXTEND
+                backend.bidirectional_block_ids = self._build_xpu_image_block_ids(
+                    forward_batch, input_ids.device
+                )
+
+    def _build_xpu_image_block_ids(self, forward_batch: ForwardBatch, device):
+        # Reads the image spans out of the sglang-specific ForwardBatch /
+        # MultimodalInputs, then delegates the framework-agnostic tensor build to
+        # sgl-kernel-xpu. This extraction stays in the model on purpose: it is
+        # sglang layout (batch fields, per-item mm offsets) and must not leak into
+        # the kernel package, which cannot import sglang types; the reusable
+        # constructor lives there as build_bidirectional_block_ids.
+        # Unique id per image span, -1 for text. The kernel indexes extend tokens
+        # only, so require full prefill (no cached prefix); return None (no mask)
+        # when a prefix is present or there are no images.
+        from sgl_kernel.flash_attn import build_bidirectional_block_ids
+
+        seq_lens, block_spans = [], []
+        for i in range(forward_batch.batch_size):
+            if int(forward_batch.extend_prefix_lens[i]) != 0:
+                return None
+            seq_lens.append(int(forward_batch.extend_seq_lens[i]))
+            spans = []
+            mm_inputs = forward_batch.mm_inputs[i]
+            if mm_inputs is not None:
+                for mm_item in mm_inputs.mm_items:
+                    if mm_item.is_image():
+                        spans.extend(mm_item.offsets)
+            block_spans.append(spans)
+        return build_bidirectional_block_ids(seq_lens, block_spans, device)
 
     def get_input_embeddings(self) -> nn.Embedding:
         return self.language_model.get_input_embeddings()
